red_flags: Unintentional weight loss or anorexia with new dyspepsia
New-onset dyspepsia after age 50, or family history of gastric cancer
Persistent vomiting or early satiety with an epigastric mass
Epigastric pain with exertional pattern, diaphoresis, or radiation to arm/jaw — treat as cardiac until ECG done
exam: Record vitals — tachycardia or hypotension raises active bleeding
Inspect conjunctivae and palmar creases for pallor (chronic blood loss)
Look for jaundice and scratch marks (biliary obstruction)
Palpate the epigastrium for tenderness and any mass
Palpate for hepatomegaly and an enlarged left supraclavicular node — either raises gastric malignancy
Perform Murphy's manoeuvre — inspiratory arrest on right-upper-quadrant pressure supports biliary disease
Percuss and palpate for splenomegaly (portal hypertension changes the bleeding differential)
Perform a digital rectal exam when bleeding is suspected — melaena on the glove settles it
Auscultate the chest and record an ECG-directed cardiac exam when the pain has any exertional flavour
Check for succussion splash hours after eating (gastric outlet obstruction from chronic ulcer or tumour)

investigations.test: H. pylori stool antigen test (off acid suppression per lab instructions)
investigations.why: First-line in uninvestigated dyspepsia WITHOUT alarm features — positive result rules in H. pylori-associated disease (ulcer, gastritis); negative shifts weight to functional dyspepsia or GERD
Iron-deficiency anaemia converts simple dyspepsia into an alarm presentation — supports bleeding ulcer or gastric malignancy and mandates endoscopy

investigations.test: ECG (and troponin if the story is acute)
investigations.why: Epigastric pain is a classic inferior-ACS presentation — an ischaemic tracing rules the cardiac mimic in; a normal ECG with troponin lets the GI pathway proceed safely in at-risk patients
Rules gallstones and biliary dilatation in or out when pain is colicky, fatty-meal-triggered, or Murphy-positive; also screens the pancreas and liver for structural disease
Raised amylase/lipase rules in pancreatitis for pain radiating to the back; abnormal LFT supports biliary obstruction over ulcer and functional disease
Longstanding diabetes with gastroparesis explains post-meal fullness and early satiety; also completes cardiac risk profiling for the ACS mimic

Second-line — mandatory if ANY alarm feature (bleeding, dysphagia, weight loss, anaemia, onset > 50, persistent vomiting) or symptoms persisting despite the first-line work-up: directly rules ulcer, oesophagitis, and gastric cancer in or out with biopsy
